text:
Isaac Howard arrived in Edmonton with a Hobey Baker Award from Michigan State and the weight of a trade: the Oilers sent Sam O'Reilly to Tampa Bay to get him. More than a year later, that deal is the story: the Edmonton Journal's notebook headline read "Sam O'Reilly shines in TB as Isaac Howard heads to Bakersfield." His last NHL game, Oct. 31 against the Islanders, lasted half a minute of ice time, and the Oilers have since sent him to the AHL.

In 13 NHL games this season he had one goal, two assists and a power-play point, on under nine minutes a night. The Oilers got 38.6% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about eight points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern in his 299 minutes last season.

The tools are still there: top speed in the 97th percentile and a shot in the 85th by NHL EDGE. Forwards picked around 31st overall usually score about 0.32 points a game in their first season of 20-plus games; he's at 0.23. At 22, Bakersfield is a chance to have the puck more.
